rows.evidence: Q1: Data and Method <U+2013> 11 monitoring wells read twice a month 2008<U+2013>2010, soil sampling in four farmlands and shelterbelts (336 samples). Q2: Results 'Variation of groundwater level', Figure 2 and Abstract (i) <U+2013> groundwater level in the drip-irrigated oasis declined on average about 0.5 m per year over the 2-year observation period, deeper in the irrigation season, which the authors attribute to the popularization/large-scale implementation of drip irrigation. Q6: Figure 2 and Abstract <U+2013> decline reported for monitoring wells distributed across Kalamiji Oasis (oasis/irrigated-zone scale, not a single plot). Q8: Discussion bullet 2 <U+2013> the link between groundwater decline 2008<U+2013>2010 and drip irrigation is stated as 'suspected' and explicitly needs further monitoring to be confirmed; Results say decline 'may be related' to drip; observation period only two years.
rows.notes: Support for the claim is observational and inferential: the study monitors groundwater under an oasis that converted to drip but has no flood-vs-drip comparison and measures no return flow or deep percolation (Q4 no). The authors themselves note confounders <U+2013> saved water was used to irrigate ~2230 ha of newly reclaimed land and farmers pump groundwater in the irrigation season <U+2013> so the decline is not cleanly attributable to reduced drip recharge. Q3 no: only well monitoring (remote sensing used for reclaimed land, not recharge). Q5 no: four wells of three textures within one oasis/climate; per-soil results not clearly reported beyond a statement that all soil types declined. Q7 no: negligible rainfall and groundwater pumping are mentioned as context, not stated as requirements. Q9 no: decline given as an average (0.5 m/yr in abstract, 0.25 m/yr in conclusions <U+2013> internally inconsistent) with no SD/CI; seasonal difference 1.0<U+2013>1.3 m is a loose range only.

notes: Full text appears complete. Internal inconsistency in the reported decline rate (0.5 m/yr in abstract/results vs 0.25 m/yr in French abstract/conclusions). Soil salinity results (shelterbelts saltier than drip-irrigated farmland) are the study's main focus but not the cited claim.
